slides.title: Key questions

paragraphs.text: Should Brightwork launch Dispatch Copilot in Q2 2027, and how should it be packaged and priced, to lift NRR from 101% to 105% by 2028 with gross margin at 75% or more?
How many customers will actually pay for Copilot, and what is it worth?
How much business does missing AI cost Brightwork today?
Which package and price close the NRR gap inside the margin floor?
Is a Q2 2027 launch worth delaying the mobile rewrite?
What must happen in 2027, and what would change the plan?
CEO and executive team, at January 2027 planning

Net revenue retention of 105% by 2028; Company gross margin stays at or above 75%; No setback to mobile reliability, the top churn reason; A launch, package and price decision at January 2027 planning
Building our own AI model; Changes to Core plan pricing; Customers outside 3–50 technician contractors

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Keep the mobile rewrite on time and launch Copilot in Q4 2027 in a Pro plan at $12 more per seat, once a paid pilot proves uptake
Copilot helps the accounts that use it, but paid demand supports at most about $2.5M of ARR, not $8M
–	14% paid at $149, against 46% stated intent in the survey
Missing AI costs at most $1.1M of ARR a year in deals and churn; mobile reliability drives 27% of churn
–	The Sales memo claims 2.8 times what the data allows
Sell Copilot in a Pro plan at $12 more per seat, with 850 requests per seat included
–	Pro needs 26% uptake; the 2023 tier reached 33%
Keep the mobile rewrite on time: delaying it risks about twice the ARR a Copilot slip would
–	A mobile delay risks $1.1M of ARR; a Copilot slip $0.6M
A paid pilot from Q2 2027 and four gates decide the package and the Q4 2027 launch
–	Pro launches only if 26% of pilot accounts pay for it

paragraphs.text: 3b: An allowance of about 850 requests per seat holds the margin floor even if typical Pro accounts use all of it
Inference budget inside the 75% margin floor, first full year with Pro at the 2023 precedent, team estimate
inference budget a year: $1.73M headroom today, plus 25% of Pro ARR, less $0.6M platform
cost a year of one request a month on all 3,234 Pro accounts
requests a month per Pro account at the floor
included requests per seat a month
The allowance is a ceiling, set well above typical use
▪	Typical use is lower: the mean beta account made 444 requests per seat, so the allowance is 1.9 times that
▪	Use above the allowance is billed at about $41 per 1,000 requests, which holds the 78% margin on the extra use
▪	Inference stays at $0.009 a request until the contract ends in December 2027
▪	Set for average 6.2-seat accounts at 33% uptake; recalibrate at the pilot gate if larger accounts or more of them move
Sources: Brightwork briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis

slides.title: 3b: Without an allowance, heavy use would push company margin below the 75% floor, as would giving Copilot away

paragraphs.text: 3b: Without an allowance, heavy use would push company margin below the 75% floor, as would giving Copilot away
Company gross margin in the first full year, %, by package and usage, team estimate
Usage, not price, decides the margin
▪	Pro, heavy use: if Pro accounts used Copilot like paywall buyers, inference would cost $2.38M a year
▪	Free in Core: fails at 1,066 requests per account a month, well under the median beta account's use
▪	Pro, base and add-on: both stay above the floor, with little room to spare
How we built the heavy-use bar
Cap included use per seat from day one and bill heavy use separately
1  Heavy use = 6,800 requests a month, the paywall buyers' average; free in Core = 1,900 requests a month on all 9,800 accounts. Includes $0.6M a year of platform cost
